name: Tsinghua University
changeSummary: Reviewed scoped record correction; historical held claims remain excluded from current policy conclusions.
summary: Tsinghua University, QS 2026 =17. This partial evidence review contains 48 source-backed claims from 15 official-source versions. Course, research, degree and student-appeal scopes are distinct. The public full AI Guiding Principles and authenticated Xiaoda entitlements remain unverified.

claimChanges.claimText: Tsinghua’s historical English feature reports Xiaoda was introduced to incoming freshmen in 2024. A September 2026 university-hosted report states it opened to all undergraduate and graduate students in June 2025. This is an institutional access statement, not permission for assessments; authenticated access and current feature entitlements were not tested.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University prohibits students from directly copying or mechanically paraphrasing AI-generated text, code, or other output and submitting it as academic coursework.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University prohibits using AI to replace academic training that graduate students are expected to complete independently, and strictly forbids AI-assisted ghostwriting, plagiarism, and fabrication in theses, dissertations, and practical achievements.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University prohibits teachers and students from using sensitive information, classified data, or unauthorized data to train or operate AI models.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University's Guiding Principles establish five core principles for AI in education: principal responsibility (AI as auxiliary tool, teachers and students as primary agents), compliance and integrity, data security, prudence and critical thinking, and fairness and inclusiveness.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University affirms that AI must remain an auxiliary tool and that teachers and students are the primary agents in teaching and learning (principal responsibility principle).

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University requires teachers and students to disclose their use of AI and AI-generated content in accordance with regulations, as part of the 'compliance and integrity' principle.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University advises instructors to determine how AI should be used according to course objectives, clearly explain AI usage norms to students at the start of each course, and remain responsible for AI-generated teaching materials.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University requires graduate supervisors to provide normative guidance on AI use and maintain full-process oversight to ensure the integrity of academic training and the originality of theses, dissertations, and practical achievements.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University urges vigilance toward AI 'hallucinations' and stresses multi-source verification to guard against cognitive complacency from overreliance on AI (prudence and critical thinking principle).

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University's Guiding Principles call for identifying and mitigating algorithmic bias and the digital divide to ensure technology serves the public good (fairness and inclusiveness principle).

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University explicitly encourages and supports faculty and students to pursue innovative applications of AI in teaching and learning, and commits to recognizing and promoting exemplary practices.

The university-hosted interview reports that when AI makes a substantive contribution to an academic outcome, students must clearly and prominently mark or declare its use as required by the university, unit or instructor. The interview is public explanatory evidence, not the retrieved full guiding-principles document.

An official-site interview explains that the AI Guiding Principles interface with the existing teaching and academic standards system rather than replace specific management rules. Units and instructors must provide the applicable implementation details.

A university-hosted report dated 29 September 2026 states Xiaoda opened to all undergraduate and graduate students in June 2025 after its 2024 freshman pilot. Account access, feature entitlements and pricing were not independently tested. This does not authorize coursework or exam use.

An undated Student Learning and Development Center page still describes Xiaoda as a pilot limited to 2024 undergraduates. This is retained as historical/conflicting page wording; the dated September 2026 report supplies the later broader opening statement. Current authenticated eligibility is untested.

The 2025 Academic Misconduct Investigation Measures apply to faculty, staff and students in academic research and related activities. They are not a universal procedure for every course-grade disagreement.

The investigation measures take effect on publication (17 November 2025) and repeal the earlier Prevention and Handling of Academic Misconduct Measures adopted in the 2016–2017 academic year. Preserve the older version as history.

For research-misconduct reports, the discipline planning office organizes preliminary verification and determines acceptance/registration within 15 working days, notifying the reporting unit or named reporter and explaining rejection in writing. Article 9 also lists grounds for non-acceptance.

Within five working days after formal registration, the university academic committee forms an investigation group of at least five and the discipline planning office gives the investigated person written notice. This deadline is for constituting a research investigation, not a student appeal.
Research fact-finding must protect the investigated person’s right to make a statement and verify the relevant facts, reasons and evidence.
Participants in academic-misconduct investigations and determinations must recuse themselves where their or relatives’ interests could affect fairness.

The university academic committee determines whether conduct is academic misconduct and its gravity from the investigation report. The university then applies the relevant rules, nature and seriousness to handling or discipline; an AI-use allegation is not an automatic sanction.

Research investigation, determination and handling should normally finish within six months of acceptance, including investigation within three months. Particularly complex cases or force majeure may justify an investigation extension approved by the academic committee chair, limited to six additional months.

Research investigations may be suspended for missing key information or unavailable conditions; suspension time is excluded. Intellectual-property litigation affecting classification requires suspension and later resumption. Death ends that person’s investigation without ending other persons’ investigations.

For ordinary degree-program students, serious homework, laboratory-report or course-paper plagiarism, alteration of laboratory data, or other serious learning falsification can attract sanctions from warning through probation under Article 21. This general framework does not classify every use of AI as misconduct.

After university academic committee determination, Article 19 assigns demerit or above for specified academic misconduct, including plagiarism, fabrication and improper authorship; plagiarism, alteration or fabrication in degree theses or published research attracts probation or above. Article 20 assigns expulsion for serious such thesis/research misconduct or thesis ghostwriting/trading. These require the specified findings and procedure.

General exam rules classify unauthorized electronic-device retrieval of exam-related materials during an exam, and the other listed carrying/copying behaviors, as cheating attracting demerit or above. This is not an AI-specific rule, not evidence of AI permission, and not an automatic sanction for any AI use.

General exam rules assign probation or above for the Article 25 categories involving obtaining or transmitting exam materials/answers or collaborative copying. Article 26 assigns expulsion for organizing cheating by three or more, impersonation, repeat cheating or other egregious cheating. Apply the actual facts and procedure, not a universal AI penalty.

The Academic Affairs Office or Graduate School is responsible for student cases involving academic misconduct or learning discipline; other categories have different competent authorities. These disciplinary regulations cover ordinary undergraduate and graduate degree students, with the specified analogous application for non-degree professional graduate students.

In student discipline, the student’s unit conducts preliminary verification and decides within five working days whether to register handling or discipline, files with the competent university authority and reports back. This is separate from the 15-working-day research-investigation acceptance stage.

Before student discipline, the proposed-sanction notice must specify the sanction type, basis, term, facts and evidence, and the rights to statement and defense. Proposed expulsion also carries a hearing-request right; students may contest the notice.

After delivery of a proposed student-sanction notice, the student, guardian or authorized representative has five working days to request written or oral statement/defense; oral requests must be arranged within five working days. Proposed expulsion carries a written hearing-request deadline of ten days after receipt, subject to the stated waiver conditions.

Demerit and lesser student sanctions are decided after leadership-office discussion; probation and expulsion require university affairs meeting determination after leadership-office discussion. Expulsion also requires prior legality review.

The student appeal measures apply to the listed university decisions on admission/student status, withdrawal, non-issuance of academic/degree certificates, and disciplinary sanctions. They do not establish a generic appeal deadline for an ordinary mark dispute.

A student contesting a decision listed in Article 3 may submit a written internal appeal within ten days of delivery of the effective decision document. If justified reasons prevented timely filing, the student may file within ten days after those reasons end. These are application deadlines, not review-completion periods.

The appeal office notifies acceptance or reasoned refusal within three working days of submitted materials. Receipt of an appeal is calculated from confirmed acceptance. The original decision generally continues during appeal; the committee may recommend deferral where necessary.

For an accepted internal student appeal, the committee normally makes a written review conclusion within fifteen days of receipt; complex cases may extend fifteen days with the chair’s approval. Receipt is defined by Article 20 as confirmed acceptance. This is not the filing deadline.
For periods under the student appeal measures, the starting day is not counted and time in transit is excluded. Do not convert the stated day periods into working days.

For degree applicants/holders, a university degree committee resolution leads to non-conferral or revocation where the degree thesis or practical achievement is determined to involve ghostwriting, plagiarism, fabrication or the other listed grounds. Before a proposed decision, the subcommittee must notify the content, facts, reasons and basis and hear statement and defense.

A degree applicant contesting an academic evaluation in expert review, defense or achievement recognition may seek written academic review from the relevant degree subcommittee. It must reorganize expert review and decide within thirty days of accepting the application; that review decision is final. The text does not supply a general thirty-day filing window.

Refusal to accept a degree application may be reviewed by the relevant unit; non-conferral or revocation may be reviewed by the university degree committee, or the person may seek legally provided external handling. The unit/committee must decide within thirty days after accepting a review application. These routes differ from academic-evaluation review.

SIGS has its own Academic Misconduct Investigation Measures, effective 1 June 2026, applying to SIGS faculty, staff and students in academic research and related activities. Do not generalize its unit procedures to every Tsinghua school.

Within SIGS, the college academic committee coordinates investigations, its research office is the secretariat, and relevant secondary units verify cases. This is the SIGS division of responsibilities, distinct from the university discipline planning office.

SIGS academic committee determines cases within its remit; cases requiring university academic committee determination are referred to the university. The college handles responsibility under the relevant school/college determination and applicable rules.
SIGS’s measures take effect on publication, dated 1 June 2026 in official metadata, and repeal the SIGS 2022 implementation rules (清深国院规〔2022〕9号).

For undergraduates under the published student-status regulations, violation of course-assessment discipline invalidates the assessment result, recorded as zero or F. This general consequence requires the relevant violation; it is not triggered by every use of AI.

The undergraduate student-status regulations provide for lawful revocation of academic/degree certificates obtained through cheating, plagiarism or other academic misconduct or improper means, and the specified registration cancellation. Degree decisions also have the distinct 2026 degree-measures procedure.

claimChanges.claimText: Tsinghua’s historical English feature reports Xiaoda was introduced to incoming freshmen in 2024. A September 2026 university-hosted report states it opened to all undergraduate and graduate students in June 2025. This is an institutional access statement, not permission for assessments; authenticated access and current feature entitlements were not tested.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University prohibits students from directly copying or mechanically paraphrasing AI-generated text, code, or other output and submitting it as academic coursework.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University prohibits using AI to replace academic training that graduate students are expected to complete independently, and strictly forbids AI-assisted ghostwriting, plagiarism, and fabrication in theses, dissertations, and practical achievements.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University prohibits teachers and students from using sensitive information, classified data, or unauthorized data to train or operate AI models.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University's Guiding Principles establish five core principles for AI in education: principal responsibility (AI as auxiliary tool, teachers and students as primary agents), compliance and integrity, data security, prudence and critical thinking, and fairness and inclusiveness.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University affirms that AI must remain an auxiliary tool and that teachers and students are the primary agents in teaching and learning (principal responsibility principle).

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University requires teachers and students to disclose their use of AI and AI-generated content in accordance with regulations, as part of the 'compliance and integrity' principle.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University advises instructors to determine how AI should be used according to course objectives, clearly explain AI usage norms to students at the start of each course, and remain responsible for AI-generated teaching materials.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University requires graduate supervisors to provide normative guidance on AI use and maintain full-process oversight to ensure the integrity of academic training and the originality of theses, dissertations, and practical achievements.

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University urges vigilance toward AI 'hallucinations' and stresses multi-source verification to guard against cognitive complacency from overreliance on AI (prudence and critical thinking principle).

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University's Guiding Principles call for identifying and mitigating algorithmic bias and the digital divide to ensure technology serves the public good (fairness and inclusiveness principle).

The university’s public news account of its AI Education Guiding Principles reports: Tsinghua University explicitly encourages and supports faculty and students to pursue innovative applications of AI in teaching and learning, and commits to recognizing and promoting exemplary practices.

The university-hosted interview reports that when AI makes a substantive contribution to an academic outcome, students must clearly and prominently mark or declare its use as required by the university, unit or instructor. The interview is public explanatory evidence, not the retrieved full guiding-principles document.

An official-site interview explains that the AI Guiding Principles interface with the existing teaching and academic standards system rather than replace specific management rules. Units and instructors must provide the applicable implementation details.

A university-hosted report dated 29 September 2026 states Xiaoda opened to all undergraduate and graduate students in June 2025 after its 2024 freshman pilot. Account access, feature entitlements and pricing were not independently tested. This does not authorize coursework or exam use.

An undated Student Learning and Development Center page still describes Xiaoda as a pilot limited to 2024 undergraduates. This is retained as historical/conflicting page wording; the dated September 2026 report supplies the later broader opening statement. Current authenticated eligibility is untested.

The 2025 Academic Misconduct Investigation Measures apply to faculty, staff and students in academic research and related activities. They are not a universal procedure for every course-grade disagreement.

The investigation measures take effect on publication (17 November 2025) and repeal the earlier Prevention and Handling of Academic Misconduct Measures adopted in the 2016–2017 academic year. Preserve the older version as history.

For research-misconduct reports, the discipline planning office organizes preliminary verification and determines acceptance/registration within 15 working days, notifying the reporting unit or named reporter and explaining rejection in writing. Article 9 also lists grounds for non-acceptance.

Within five working days after formal registration, the university academic committee forms an investigation group of at least five and the discipline planning office gives the investigated person written notice. This deadline is for constituting a research investigation, not a student appeal.
Research fact-finding must protect the investigated person’s right to make a statement and verify the relevant facts, reasons and evidence.
Participants in academic-misconduct investigations and determinations must recuse themselves where their or relatives’ interests could affect fairness.

The university academic committee determines whether conduct is academic misconduct and its gravity from the investigation report. The university then applies the relevant rules, nature and seriousness to handling or discipline; an AI-use allegation is not an automatic sanction.

Research investigation, determination and handling should normally finish within six months of acceptance, including investigation within three months. Particularly complex cases or force majeure may justify an investigation extension approved by the academic committee chair, limited to six additional months.

Research investigations may be suspended for missing key information or unavailable conditions; suspension time is excluded. Intellectual-property litigation affecting classification requires suspension and later resumption. Death ends that person’s investigation without ending other persons’ investigations.

For ordinary degree-program students, serious homework, laboratory-report or course-paper plagiarism, alteration of laboratory data, or other serious learning falsification can attract sanctions from warning through probation under Article 21. This general framework does not classify every use of AI as misconduct.

After university academic committee determination, Article 19 assigns demerit or above for specified academic misconduct, including plagiarism, fabrication and improper authorship; plagiarism, alteration or fabrication in degree theses or published research attracts probation or above. Article 20 assigns expulsion for serious such thesis/research misconduct or thesis ghostwriting/trading. These require the specified findings and procedure.

General exam rules classify unauthorized electronic-device retrieval of exam-related materials during an exam, and the other listed carrying/copying behaviors, as cheating attracting demerit or above. This is not an AI-specific rule, not evidence of AI permission, and not an automatic sanction for any AI use.

General exam rules assign probation or above for the Article 25 categories involving obtaining or transmitting exam materials/answers or collaborative copying. Article 26 assigns expulsion for organizing cheating by three or more, impersonation, repeat cheating or other egregious cheating. Apply the actual facts and procedure, not a universal AI penalty.

The Academic Affairs Office or Graduate School is responsible for student cases involving academic misconduct or learning discipline; other categories have different competent authorities. These disciplinary regulations cover ordinary undergraduate and graduate degree students, with the specified analogous application for non-degree professional graduate students.

In student discipline, the student’s unit conducts preliminary verification and decides within five working days whether to register handling or discipline, files with the competent university authority and reports back. This is separate from the 15-working-day research-investigation acceptance stage.

Before student discipline, the proposed-sanction notice must specify the sanction type, basis, term, facts and evidence, and the rights to statement and defense. Proposed expulsion also carries a hearing-request right; students may contest the notice.

After delivery of a proposed student-sanction notice, the student, guardian or authorized representative has five working days to request written or oral statement/defense; oral requests must be arranged within five working days. Proposed expulsion carries a written hearing-request deadline of ten days after receipt, subject to the stated waiver conditions.

Demerit and lesser student sanctions are decided after leadership-office discussion; probation and expulsion require university affairs meeting determination after leadership-office discussion. Expulsion also requires prior legality review.

The student appeal measures apply to the listed university decisions on admission/student status, withdrawal, non-issuance of academic/degree certificates, and disciplinary sanctions. They do not establish a generic appeal deadline for an ordinary mark dispute.

A student contesting a decision listed in Article 3 may submit a written internal appeal within ten days of delivery of the effective decision document. If justified reasons prevented timely filing, the student may file within ten days after those reasons end. These are application deadlines, not review-completion periods.

The appeal office notifies acceptance or reasoned refusal within three working days of submitted materials. Receipt of an appeal is calculated from confirmed acceptance. The original decision generally continues during appeal; the committee may recommend deferral where necessary.

For an accepted internal student appeal, the committee normally makes a written review conclusion within fifteen days of receipt; complex cases may extend fifteen days with the chair’s approval. Receipt is defined by Article 20 as confirmed acceptance. This is not the filing deadline.
For periods under the student appeal measures, the starting day is not counted and time in transit is excluded. Do not convert the stated day periods into working days.

For degree applicants/holders, a university degree committee resolution leads to non-conferral or revocation where the degree thesis or practical achievement is determined to involve ghostwriting, plagiarism, fabrication or the other listed grounds. Before a proposed decision, the subcommittee must notify the content, facts, reasons and basis and hear statement and defense.
